summary: A notice from Alex McKenzie about address changes after the RAND IMP was temporarily removed and a new IMP installed at ISI. The RAND TENEX became the ISI TENEX. It gives new addresses, one of which was corrected in RFC 405.

plainLanguage.summary: A group of people and their computer moved to a new building, so this note gives the new addresses.

questions: rand to isi host address change
subtitle: A short notice about the RAND IMP removal and the new ISI IMP, with the host addresses that changed.

tldr.problem: People and computers moved from RAND to ISI, and the RAND IMP was removed from the network for a time, so network addresses changed.
tldr.mechanism: The notice says a new IMP, number 86, was installed at ISI, where the former RAND TENEX is now Host number one and so has Network Address 86.
tldr.outcome: The RAND IMP was due to be re-installed early the next week as IMP number 7, keeping address 7 for the IBM 360/65. RFC 405 is listed as updating this notice.

today: The metadata lists no formal status for RFC 404, and it says the notice is updated by RFC 405. It is a one-page notice of address changes from 1972 and has no ongoing protocol role.

sections.title: What Moved
sections.content: This week the RAND IMP was temporarily removed from the network and a new IMP was installed at ISI. Some of the people and computers from RAND moved to ISI. In particular, the RAND TENEX is now the ISI TENEX.
sections.plainLanguage: A computer and some of its people moved from one place to another, and the network got a new connection point where they went.

sections.title: The New Network Address
sections.content: The address of the ISI IMP is 86 (decimal), and the TENEX at ISI is Host number one. So the Network Address of the ISI TENEX is 86. In this notice a host's Network Address is simply the number of the IMP it hangs off, taken as the address.
sections.plainLanguage: The new building has the number 86. Because the moved computer is the first one inside, its address is just 86.

sections.title: The RAND IMP Returns
sections.content: Sometime early the following week the RAND IMP will be re-installed. It will still be IMP number 7, and the IBM 360/65 at RAND will still have Network Address 7. Only the TENEX and its people changed place; RAND's other computer keeps the address it had.
sections.plainLanguage: The old building gets its connection back soon with the same number as before, so its remaining computer keeps its old address.
